plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to meet concentration limits and reduce risk.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SMH, SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, METU) to zero for capital preservation.
This plan prioritizes safety by removing high-risk, below-stop positions.
It aims for a stable, low-drawdown portfolio.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating all leveraged ETFs and trimming concentrated positions. Expect lower volatility and smaller drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to align with concentration limits.
Sell SMH entirely due to being below its stop and to reduce sector risk.
Trim other leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to smaller, more manageable positions.
This approach balances growth potential with a focus on risk management.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while maintaining some exposure to growth assets. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a reasonable growth outlook.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet concentration limits.
Sell SMH entirely as it is below its stop and to free up capital.
Buy TECS, TZA, SPXS, and DRIP, which are strong scanner setups, to increase aggressive exposure.
This plan leans into leverage and high-scoring setups for stretched growth potential.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It utilizes leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring scanner setups. Be aware that this approach significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk, and leveraged ETFs are subject to daily decay and rebalancing.

plan: Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income generation.
Sell all high-beta and leveraged ETFs (SMH, SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, METU) to near zero.
This strategy prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
It aims to park cash for yield rather than aggressive growth.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown by rotating into income-focused ETFs and cutting high-beta, leveraged positions. While aiming for stability, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
